text:
**Best overall combo: BLUETTI AC200L + ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W folding panel**, about **$1,123** with codes.

- [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l): $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF.
  - 2,048 Wh LiFePO4 battery, rated for 3,000+ cycles.
  - 2,400 W continuous output, with a built-in TT-30 RV outlet.
  - Accepts up to 1,200 W of solar, so you can add panels later.
  - Expandable to 8,192 Wh. Weighs 28.3 kg (about 62 lb).
- [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel): $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26.
  - Its 45.3 V open-circuit voltage is within the AC200L's 12–145 V solar input range.
  - IP67 rated, with adapters included. It's heavy for a folding panel at 18.5 kg.

Source: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rv-portable-power-station-solar-panel-combo-2026-comparison-ecoflow-bluetti)

**Caveats**
- Dealectric only covers BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS. It has no EcoFlow or Jackery data, so this isn't a full three-brand comparison.
- Those links are affiliate links, and the codes were last tested on Oct 21, 2026, so confirm the prices at checkout.
- The two items come from different stores, so you'll check out twice.
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). The AC200L's surge rating is 3,600 W, so starting a roof AC is borderline. Plan on a soft-start kit or a bigger unit if you want AC off-grid.
- For sizing, a 150 W fridge running 10 hours uses about 1,500 Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)). One 2 kWh unit covers a fridge, lights, and electronics, but not much more.

**Alternatives**
- **More capacity, stays put in the RV:** [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) has 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W at 120 V, and an RV outlet. It's $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12, or $1,588.22 with one SP037. It weighs 45 kg, so it isn't hand-carry.
- **Roughly 3 kWh with a long cycle life:** [BLUETTI Elite 300](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-300) has 3,014 Wh, 6,000+ cycles, and a TT-30 outlet. It's $1,199 with no working code. It was on pre-order, shipping from Oct 23, and it can't be expanded.
- **Full-time boondocking with AC:** EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W, 8,000 W surge) was the top pick in [EmergencyEnergy's comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). It's heavy, and the most expensive once you add expansion batteries. The Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024 Wh, 3,000 W) is their pick for running AC. The search results didn't include direct purchase links for either, so use that article's price links. That site is Ontario-based, so its electrical-code notes may not apply to you.

**Skip for an RV:** the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (no RV outlet listed) and the small 300 Wh units.

If you tell me whether you need to run a roof AC and how many days you'll boondock, I can narrow this to one pick.
